title: Hard Pretzels with Peanut Butter Filling

content.title: About
content.content: Hard pretzels with a peanut butter filling are salty, knot‑shaped baked snacks with a crisp outer crust and a smooth, slightly sweet peanut butter center. They combine the crunch of traditional pretzel dough with the richness of roasted peanuts.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Classic German pretzels are made from a simple dough, but modern versions often add flavorings and fillings.
The peanut butter filling is usually made from roasted peanuts, salt, and a touch of sugar.
The crisp crust is achieved by a double‑baking process: the dough is first boiled in a lye solution, then baked until golden.
Pretzels are commonly served with beer, but they also make a quick energy snack in school lunchboxes.
In the United States, over 200 million packages of flavored pretzels are sold each year.

items.title: Rich in protein
items.content: Peanut butter provides about 25 g of protein per 100 g, supporting muscle maintenance.

items.title: Source of healthy fats
items.content: Monounsaturated and polyunsaturated fats in peanuts promote heart health when consumed in moderation.

items.title: Contains vitamin E
items.content: Vitamin E acts as an antioxidant, protecting cells from oxidative damage.

items.title: Provides iron
items.content: Peanut butter supplies iron, essential for oxygen transport in the blood.

items.title: Sustains energy
items.content: The combination of carbohydrates from the dough and fats from the peanut butter offers lasting satiety.

items.title: Peanut allergy
items.content: These pretzels can trigger severe allergic reactions in individuals sensitive to peanuts.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: The salty crust may be unsuitable for people with hypertension; low‑salt versions are recommended.

items.title: Calorie dense
items.content: Because of the fats in the filling and carbs in the dough, the snack is relatively high in calories; portion control is advised.

items.title: Choking hazard for young children
items.content: The hard texture can pose a choking risk for small kids; offer broken pieces or smaller portions.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Enjoy pretzels straight from the bag, crumble them into salads, use as a base for appetizers, or dip them in cheese or yogurt sauces. They can also be broken and drizzled with chocolate for a sweet twist.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep in an airtight container in a cool, dry place. For longer shelf life, store in the refrigerator to prevent fat oxidation. Discard if you notice a rancid smell or texture changes.
